not_yet_implemented_by_this_Rust_slice.family: XER and JER outside supported slices
not_yet_implemented_by_this_Rust_slice.note: XER supports only basic encoding of flat SET and SEQUENCE records with untagged or automatic-tagged direct BOOLEAN, bounded INTEGER, and unconstrained IA5String, and REAL DEFAULT 0.5 fields with finite limited values; decoding and mixed codec selection are unsupported. JER is qualified for listed primitives and strings.

not_yet_implemented_by_this_Rust_slice.family: constructed outside nested UPER SEQUENCE, extensible, fragmented or disjoint strings, named-bit strings, CHOICE, extensible ENUMERATED, REAL, open types
not_yet_implemented_by_this_Rust_slice.note: No Rust correctness or interoperability claim is made beyond the listed INTEGER, SEQUENCE, and bounded string subsets.
Extension and cross-codec policies remain unqualified.
UPER and CER methods are selected independently; CER decoding is strict (canonical input only).

comparison_policy.C_role: Current C implementation is a comparison implementation, not a protocol oracle.
comparison_policy.independent_checks: Rust fixed vectors, malformed-input checks, budgets, and round trips
comparison_policy.canonicality: CER claims cover listed vectors only. Bit counts cover full TLVs. IA5 BER preserves bytes; CER enforces its 7-bit alphabet.
